strengths.label: Four closed theoremlets on one audited-shell package
strengths.note: Lawfulness, cocycle pressure closure, strict theory extension, and conditional disintegration are all frozen in one package.

strengths.label: Canonical hybrid object is explicit
strengths.note: The branch no longer relies on an unstable object definition; the hybrid object is intrinsic and factorization-based.

strengths.label: Scope firewall is already frozen
strengths.note: Traceability and claim-ledger artifacts make overclaiming materially harder.

strengths.label: Paper-native thermodynamic consequence route closed
strengths.note: Conditional disintegration replaced the conceptually wrong direct stratumwise route.

risks.label: Audited-shell-only scope
risks.mitigation: State the class as audited-shell only everywhere and block any shell-general phrasing.
risks.note: The package is strong on the audited shell but intentionally does not generalize to broader shells.

risks.label: No broader-class theorem
risks.mitigation: Keep broader-class ambitions in reserve-only language and do not market the result as a class-expansion theorem.
risks.note: Reviewer resistance will rise if the paper implies family breadth rather than audited-shell closure.

risks.label: No external/non-SFT breadth claim
risks.mitigation: Avoid universality rhetoric and keep non-SFT comparisons out of the core claim set.
risks.note: The package is six-birds-native and continuous, but not an external breadth theorem.

risks.label: Canonical hybrid object complexity
risks.mitigation: Use the frozen theorem summary and traceability matrix to keep the object definition tight and repeatable.
risks.note: A serious reviewer may find the hybrid object technically dense even if the internal package is coherent.

risks.label: Dependence on the continuous-kernel reset rather than older discrete families
risks.mitigation: Frame the reset as a deliberate branch reset and distinguish it cleanly from the earlier delayed/finite families.
risks.note: Some readers may prefer the older discrete baselines and treat the reset as a change of arena rather than a theorem advance.

risks.label: Possible reviewer read of the result as adapted from PICA
risks.mitigation: Separate inherited substrate semantics from the new theoremlets and canonical hybrid closure in every internal summary.
risks.note: The vendor repo supplies substrate machinery and primitive semantics, so novelty has to be argued at the theorem-package level.

risks.label: Strict extension theoremlet may look too shell-specific
risks.mitigation: Keep the claim on the audited shell and present the shell restriction as part of the theorem object rather than as a hidden weakness.
risks.note: The theoremlet is real, but a reviewer could still question how much of it survives outside the audited shell.

risks.label: Conditional disintegration may be read as too proxy-based if overstated
risks.mitigation: Claim the weighted package-conditioned pressure gap theoremlet only; mention KL-style closure-deficit proxies as support-only.
risks.note: Overstating the KL or exact information-theoretic layer would create avoidable reviewer pushback.

risks.label: Rejected routes may confuse reviewers about what is actually claimed
risks.mitigation: Keep the rejected broader-class and stratumwise routes explicit as non-claims, not as partial claims.
risks.note: The branch contains several honest negative results that need to be framed as scope discipline rather than failed core claims.

objection_map.objection: The theorem package is only on a narrow audited shell.
objection_map.response: That scope is explicit, frozen, and traceable; the package does not claim more than it closes.

objection_map.objection: This looks like an adaptation of vendor substrate work rather than a new theorem package.
objection_map.response: The substrate reset is adapted, but the closed theoremlets, canonical hybrid object, strict extension, and conditional disintegration package are new in this branch.

objection_map.objection: The thermodynamic consequence is too proxy-based.
objection_map.response: The closed claim is only the weighted package-conditioned pressure gap theoremlet; KL-style closure-deficit language is support-only.

objection_map.objection: The object is too complicated and the route changes are hard to follow.
objection_map.response: The canonical object, traceability matrix, and non-claim firewall keep the final package auditable despite the development history.

claim_posture.manuscript_posture: State a Level-3 core on the audited shell, emphasize the canonical hybrid object and strict theory extension, and keep broader-scope ambitions outside the paper-core claim set.

notes: The package is publication-ready only under conservative audited-shell claim discipline.
The six-birds papers directory is absent from this snapshot, so the prior-paper baseline uses the in-repo vendor six-birds materials plus earlier internal theorem branches.
